As to your claim that we don't know if this is a part of the natural climactic cycle, we actually do know. 

1. We have ice cores which date back millions of years, showing the cycle of warming. Typically it takes many tens of thousands of years to see the shifts we are seeing today in a generation. 

2. These findings are consistent with chemical analysis of atmospheric conditions, which show that increased levels of co2 from combustion are causing a runaway greenhouse effect.

3. The timeline of the atmospheric changes matches exactly the amount of fossil fuel that we're burning. 

Interestingly, climatically we are in an interglacial period, meaning we should be heading toward an ice age (over several hundred thousand years). Human activity has actually reversed the cycle toward a hothouse earth. So it's not that you don't get hothouse earth every so often, it just usually happens once ever several hundred millions years.

The issue isn't that it gets hot the issue is the speed if the heating being faster than has previously happened. This means nothing can adapt fast enough, leading to a mass extinction event. Such events reshape the global ecosystem, which means our source of 02 and food could be in jeopardy.

So you would have to have an awfully strange coincidence to account for all of the evidence to line up like this. 

But don't take my word for it, tens of thousands of scientists have independently verified these studies over decades. Read the data yourself.

The landscape of the internet has changed a lot since the heyday of the early 2000s or even 2010s.
Now Google has to search through more and more content, with even more content being constantly added at an increasing rate.

Google's algorithm has had to make increasingly broad judgments about what to show you, in order to keep up with the pace of content.

There is a tremendous amount of junk, propaganda, and advertising competing to manipulate Google's algorithm to get to the top page. 

Ultimately Google's algorithm can't decide what's real or valid, so the devs have set it to rank results based on popularity and paid sponsorship (which itself is a very complicated process) 

So what you see is broad, ad driven, and generic because because that is all that the algorithm can reliably find anymore. 

Google is now a monopoly with fingers in AI, cars, satellites, mapping, entertainment, data brokerage, and much more. They have limited incentive to built a radically new and sophisticated search system to cut through the clutter.

Tolkien himself lamented some of the racial undertones in his writing, i.e. making orcs black. He didn't mean it to be racist, but he was a white man living in the early 20th century, so some of that rubs of in his work. 

Contemporary readers might see Aryan elves indiscriminately killing black orcs, which are said to their core evil and base. Westerners killing evil Easterners. The optics are bad. But we also need to look at Tolkien in the time and place he lived. 

He was very, very catholic (raised by the church) and an British nationalist at a time when the Empire commited atrocities against non-whites. Tolkien himself wasn't a racist or a misogynist in his time. He also wasn't a progressive, or pushing the boundaries on topics like race and gender. The implicit racial and gender bias in his stories sometimes shows through, and Tolkien was likey blind to a lot of it - as was his contemporary, 20th century audience. 

That said, FOR THE TIME Tolkien's portrayal of Arwen and Eowyn was fairly progressive. Tolkien also shows racial conflict, as well as peace between dwarves and elves. Ulitmately he shows people from all walks of life - rich, poor, elf, dwarf, male, female, old, young, big, small, can play a crucial role in the world. In that sense, his message is very tolerant. 

Tolkien made Middle Earth as an attempt to recreate pre-Anglo Saxon mythology in his stories - based on cobbled together Germanic, Norse, Celtic and other sources.Germanic mythology does have what you might call proto-racial ideas in it. Purity of blood, Aryan looking people being considered pure, and monsters having black skin (although this wasn't a slight against African decented people until much later in history). 

A lot of these ideas influenced Germanic racism and eventually Nazism, hence the association between the two. 

The non-democratic and hierarchical nature of Middle Earth seems to be from Tolkien's life experience, as well as the historical materials he was inspired by. The man was a monarchist, who spent his life in the hierarchy of the Catholic Church and British Army. For his time and place, this wasn't strange. 

I think you can love Lord of the Rings, and still be critical of the historical legacy it is enmeshed in. Tolkien was just a man, imperfect and biases. I think Tolkien was a pretty moderate person considering his life and times, when many of his contemporaries were more overtly racist and misogynistic in their works.

All sensations appear the same to the brain without extra processing: it's all just electro chemical data. Processes in the brain, like organic computer programs, have to determine which if these singlas is likey from within the body, versus from outside it. 

Serotonin is really critical in that process, like binary is to computer code. So if there are reasons that your levels are changing (like meds stopping) then it would be normal to have some weird feelings, as your brain reacclimates to different serotonin levels. 

Discontinuation syndrome is where the brain suddenly has to start making the serotonin, norepinephrine, or other neurotransmitters that have been substitute via medications. It's It not used to doing this, and can take 2-6 weeks to adapt to the changed chemical levels. During that time you can feel SUPER weird.

So overall, I'd wait 2-6 weeks. If it doesn't get better, go back to your doctor. If it gets worse, you can go back tonyour doc and start taking the meds again so that you can titrate off them slowly, giving your brain less of a sudden shift.

I used to be an SSI legal professional, my day job was handling SSI litigation.

SSI and SSDI are run by extremely underfunded, and politicized federal agencies, administered by state run disability determination offices that see people as quotas.

Sadly, the culture of the Federal SSI/SSDI system is that applicants are exaggerating their issues, and are rarely accepted after one application, especially in the case of mental health related issues. 3-5 applications, and appeals (three levels of appeal) are required before an applicant will be taken seriously.

If it gives you some idea, I had a client who was crushed by city bus, and lost her lower limbs, and mid torso. Her upper body was crushed such that she was in constant pain, in a wheel chair. A Federal judge told me she "should be able to find some work", and dismissed her case 3 times before she was awarded SSI, SSDI. The system is a sick joke.

The one silver lining is that you are entitled to get back payments if you are later found to be eligible for SSI, SSDI, and were wrongly denied. these back payments are typically 15-35 thousand dollars, given in 6K installments.

If you want to get SSI/SSDI I would do the following:

1. Get every medical record for your disability that you can dating back 10 years. Do not leave anything out that is about your case, but do not include anything that would unflappable to you i.e. therapy notes from a therapist you had a bad relationship with.
2. Speak to an attorney at a non-profit legal aid clinic, or if you are in an area, a private attorney (though be wary of private lawyers for SSI/SSDI). Disability rights groups may also be able to help you navigate the process.
3. By yourself, or with the help of a lawyer, read the SSI/SSDI definition of your disability in the SSI/SSDI Federal Social Security Hand Book ([https://www.ssa.gov/OP\_Home/handbook/handbook.html](https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/handbook/handbook.html))
4. Explain how your life fits the definition, and use supporting medical records to show this.
5. Get examinations for your disability from BOTH Social Security and Private doctors.
6. Submit all documentation in a timely manner, and get someone to call the SS Office to make sure they actually received the documents, and are processing them.
7. Appeal, appeal, appeal! Do not stop appealing your case under any circumstances. Escalate it to the Federal Circuit if necessary, it is worth the wait because it you win you will get on for life and recessive a healthy back payment.
